description: Asking for approval, sending it through each interface, the company's checks in order, new revisions, who can approve, and at most once.

cases.description: A request for an action that needs approval is refused: HTTP 403 with error approval_required and the operation, nothing performed; the API description says so.
The same request for the same terms returns the same revision.
The same request with Poppy-Approval is performed, and answered as it would have been without operations.
A retry with the same approval after the outcome gets the original response; the action is performed once.
While the outcome is unknown, the request and its retries get HTTP 503 and Retry-After, never a failure, and the action is performed once.
An approval of a revision the company replaced performs nothing and gets a new revision of the same operation, never the one it named; that one, approved, is performed.
An approval of a revision the company never returned performs nothing and gets a new revision.
An approval sent with another request than the one that returned the operation performs nothing and gets a new revision.
Members of Poppy-Approval the company doesn't recognize are ignored.
A Poppy-Approval that isn't a Dictionary with both members as Strings is a request without an approval.
An approval after expires_at performs nothing and gets a new revision of the same operation.
An operation returned signed in can be approved in any Session of the same personal agent and user, signed in to the account.
A signed-out Session of the same personal agent and user gets a challenge for the account.
A Session that can't approve the operation is handled as if it had no approval.
The same action through the API and then a conversation is the same operation ID.
The same action through an MCP tool, in structuredContent.operation of an error result, is the same operation as through the API.
The same tool call with _meta approval is performed; a retry gets the original result.
A message's text approves nothing, whatever it says.
A message with approval is performed, and a later company message says how it went; a new message with the same approval adds nothing.
A request whose answer is lost is sent again with the same approval, performed once.
An action that failed partway says what it changed, and a retry gets the same answer.
